text:
kira: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a couple of clarifying asks on GPU provisioning / region overflow behavior when supply tightens. TL;DR: what is the routing precedence when a region hits capacity?

sam: short answer: precedence is (1) local reserved pools (Dedicated), (2) same-region shared capacity, (3) configured spillover regions (in configured priority order), (4) global best-effort pool. cross-continent routing is opt-in per account.

michelle: adding one nuance — Dedicated contracts are isolated by default. if a customer enables 'cross-region failover' we prefer their reserved capacity in the target region over shared capacity. SLA and billing treatment differ in that case.

raj: ops note: during spillover we automatically reduce allowed max_seq_len for latency-sensitive routes and prefer an int8/quantized variant to keep p95 under target. we tag traces with routing=spillover and include original_region and target_region.

kira: thanks. timeline Q: when will APAC get the additional zone + configured spillover pair? any ETA we can communicate to customers?

sam: target is end of Q3 for the extra APAC zone, but it's contingent on hardware arrival and networking approvals. i have procurement sync Wed — will post a firm date after that.

vlad: for Dedicated customers under active contracts — will they get advance notice before cross-region failovers or tests? we need an opt-out path for legal/compliance customers.

michelle: yes — planned cross-region failover tests will have 72h pre-notice for Dedicated customers with opt-out. emergency spillover (supply outage) will be followed by an incident timeline + optional credits if SLA impacted.

ops-bot: playbook updated: https://internal.redwood/infra/playbooks/region-spillover — includes runbooks, dashboards, and the tagging schema :robot_face:

jamie: action items: @sam — confirm APAC ETA after procurement sync; @raj — add routing=spillover & original_region to all traces and ensure logs are searchable; i'll draft a customer-facing FAQ for next week.

sam: noted, i'll update the product and sales channels and post an internal FAQ once dates are firm.

michelle: also flagging: Redwood Optimize auto-batching may adjust batch sizes when routing changes; we'll coordinate with eng teams to avoid QoS regressions.

kira: perfect — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
